name: UK Garage / 2-Step
summary: 2-step kick on 1 plus syncopated 16ths (beat 3 left empty), snare or clap locked to 2 and 4, and swung 16th hats with heavy MPC-style accent contour. Rim ghosts, skippy kicks and offbeat open hats fill the pocket; the modern revival tightens the swing, weights the kick and adds ascending rim runs.

sounds.kick: Short, punchy MPC/909-style kick, often pitched up 2–3 semitones so the sub-bass owns the low end; classic tracks add a deeper 808 kick as a second layer.
sounds.snare: Composite snare: a snappy electronic layer (Alesis-style) plus an 808 snare pitched up for crack, or a clap+snare stack; rim shots (707/808-style, one reverbed) carry the skips.
sounds.hats: Short closed hat with the attack softened, a slightly longer hat or cabasa for offbeats, open hat between closed and open in decay; MPC swing 60–69%.
sounds.percussion: Live-sounding shaker and tambourine with real velocity contour, congas for the organic lane, chopped Amen slices in the revival.
sounds.cymbals: One crash at phrase starts only; ride rarely, and then quiet and high-passed.

machines: Akai MPC60 / MPC3000 — the swing engine and sample chopper of classic 2-step (owned)
Roland TR-909 — kick and open hat foundation (owned)
Roland TR-808 — pitched-up snare/clap layer, deep kick layer (owned)
LinnDrum / Sequential DrumTraks — 80s-machine snares and claps cited in Attack's dissection (owned)
Korg M1 drums — the organ-era garage kit (owned)
Alesis DM5 — snappy composite snare layer (get elsewhere)
Ensoniq EPS — Todd Edwards' sampler; approximate with Akai S900 (owned) 12-bit crunch
Breakbeat libraries (Amen) — sliced and re-pitched in revival garage (owned)
references: Artful Dodger feat. Craig David — Re-Rewind (1999)
Interplanetary Criminal — B.O.T.A. (Baddest Of Them All) (2022)
